paragraphs.text: A small Dodecanese island that quietly became one of Europe's best sport climbing destinations — steep grey limestone dripping with tufas and stalactites, set right above a genuinely turquoise Aegean.
Routes here reward technical, three-dimensional movement over raw power, with a huge spread of grades packed into a small area — ideal for a course built around real, measurable progression.

practicalCards.heading: Accommodation
practicalCards.body: Shared accommodation in local climbing hostels, cottages, or places run by local climbers. Want something more comfortable? Send us a personal inquiry by email or WhatsApp.

practicalCards.heading: Getting There
practicalCards.body: Fly into Kos, then a short ferry across to Kalymnos. Local transport on the island is organised once you land.

practicalCards.heading: Gear
practicalCards.body: All safety equipment provided — ropes, draws, helmets, slings. Bring your own shoes and harness if you have preferences; we've got spares if you don't.

practicalCards.heading: Group Size
practicalCards.body: up to 8 participants, max 7:1 coach ratio. Minimum 3 to run the course — otherwise we offer an equivalent alternative or a full refund.

children.text: Kalymnos is basically what happens when a Greek island decides to be made entirely of climbable limestone — steep walls, hanging tufas, and stalactite features that turn every route into a three-dimensional puzzle.

Two weeks of daily coaching from Sergi and Miha, covering everything from proper belaying and clipping tactics to redpoint mindset and overhang technique — whatever's actually holding your climbing back.
Small enough group ratios (max 7:1) that you're never just another face in the crowd, big enough energy that the evenings are just as memorable as the days.

faqs.question: What level do I need to be?
faqs.answer: Previous outdoor sport climbing experience is highly recommended, at a minimum of indoor leading 6a or outdoor leading 5. This course suits climbers from strong beginners to advanced, and it's open to ages 15 and up.

faqs.question: Do I need my own gear?
faqs.answer: Bring climbing shoes and a harness you trust. We provide belay devices, helmets, and slings, plus a full kit list once you book (down jacket, headlamp, sleeping bag, and a backpack for crag days).

faqs.question: Is food included?
faqs.answer: Food arrangements and any included meals are confirmed before departure.

faqs.question: What if fewer than 3 people book?
faqs.answer: We need a minimum of 3 participants to run the course. If numbers don't add up, we'll offer an equivalent (or better) alternative trip, or a full refund. No hard feelings.

faqs.question: Can I book just one week?
faqs.answer: Yes — each week runs individually at €1,090. This page covers the full 2-week option at €1,890; see the schedule above for single-week dates.

faqs.question: Where do I fly in and out of?
faqs.answer: Kos International Airport, followed by a short ferry crossing to Kalymnos.

coachProfiles.bio: Born and raised around Barcelona's best crags — Montserrat, Siurana, Margalef — Sergi has been climbing for 25 years and now splits his time between Greece and Spain, leading courses and trips across both.

A late starter who progressed to onsighting 7c within three years, Miha left a career in research writing to become a certified climbing instructor and guide, bringing a genuinely science-minded approach to coaching mental barriers.
